title: Bayern Munich Sells Final 5% Stake to Viessmann Family for €250 Million
excerpt: The deal brings Max Viessmann's investment group into the ownership structure of one of football's most valuable clubs, valuing Bayern Munich AG at €5 billion.
body:
• Bayern Munich is selling its remaining 5% stake in FC Bayern AG for €250 million, implying a total club valuation of €5 billion
  • The buyer is Max Viessmann's Viessmann Generations Group, a Munich-based private equity firm — not the existing corporate partner Viessmann Climate Solutions
  • The Viessmann family sold its climate solutions division to Carrier Global in 2023 for approximately €12 billion
  • Bayern's members' association retains 70% of the club, with Adidas, Audi, and Allianz each holding 8.33%

A New Name in Bayern's Ownership Circle

Bayern Munich is set to sell the final 5% stake in FC Bayern AG for approximately €250 million, bringing the Viessmann family directly into the ownership structure of Germany's most successful football club, according to a report by Bild.

The buyer is not Viessmann Climate Solutions, which has served as Bayern's Platinum Partner, but rather Max Viessmann's Viessmann Generations Group, a Munich-based private equity and investment firm. The distinction matters: this is a personal investment by the Viessmann family, not a corporate sponsorship extension.

The Viessmann Fortune

The Viessmann family's financial firepower stems from the 2023 sale of its climate solutions division to U.S.-based Carrier Global for approximately €12 billion. Since then, Max Viessmann has deployed a significant portion of the proceeds into sustainable ecosystems, co-investments, and equity stakes through Viessmann Generations Group.

Bayern Munich represents the latest — and arguably most prominent — addition to that portfolio. Max Viessmann has served on the Administrative Advisory Board of FC Bayern e.V. since spring 2026, solidifying a connection that started in the commercial space and is now evolving into an ownership stake.

What the Deal Means for Bayern

The €250 million price tag for 5% implies Bayern Munich AG is valued at €5 billion, making it one of the most valuable football clubs in the world. The club's ownership structure has long been distinctive in European football: the members' association holds at least 70% of the spinoff company that runs the football operations, in keeping with Germany's 50+1 rule.

The remaining 25% has been split equally among three long-standing corporate partners — Adidas, Audi, and Allianz — each holding approximately 8.33%. The final 5% had remained available under Bayern's statutes but was never sold until now.

"A partnership that started in the commercial space could now become a much deeper relationship."

— Bavarian Football Works

A Calculated Move

For Bayern, the sale brings fresh capital without diluting the members' association below its constitutionally mandated 70% threshold. Earlier this year, talks between Bayern and Swedish private equity firm EQT over a potential minority stake reportedly collapsed after CFO Michael Diederich left the club for Deutsche Bank, according to the Financial Times.

The Viessmann deal avoids some of the political sensitivities that accompany outside private equity investment in German football. Widespread fan protests prompted the Bundesliga to abandon talks over a league-wide PE investment in 2024, and honorary president Uli Hoeneß's calls for rethinking the 50+1 rule remain controversial.

By selling to a family with existing ties to the club rather than an external financial firm, Bayern may have found the path of least resistance to unlocking additional capital as it prepares for the 2026/27 Bundesliga season.
